tldr: Trump publicly rejected Iran's seven-day Hormuz roadmap Saturday and told aides he expects to resume bombing Iran after the November midterms -- a materially harder line than Friday's truce-hope framing, and the single biggest swing factor for markets heading into Monday's open.

Oil already reversed higher into Sunday's Globex reopen (Brent ~$103, WTI ~$97, both up 1.5-2% from Friday) on the rejection headline, while a separate Iran-Gulf-states meeting on Hormuz terms was also postponed over the weekend -- both point toward the ~Mon-Tue deadline lapsing without a deal.

regime.oneLiner: Trump's weekend rejection of Iran's Hormuz roadmap makes a clean resolution by Monday-Tuesday's deadline look less likely, not more, even as equities closed Friday pricing calm.

topNews.headline: Trump publicly rejects Iran's seven-day Hormuz roadmap, expects to resume bombing after midterms
topNews.actionable: This reverses Friday's truce-hope framing -- expect Monday's Asia open to price renewed war-premium risk, not de-escalation; keep the silver/gold-miner sleeve sized for escalation into the deadline rather than a quiet rollover.

topNews.headline: Oil reverses higher after Trump's rejection headline; Hormuz traffic still 'at a standstill'
topNews.actionable: The real-yield headwind that pressured gold/silver miners Friday may be partly offset by a firmer war-premium bid into Monday -- don't extrapolate Friday's oil pullback into this week.

topNews.headline: Bitcoin drops ~3.8% then partly recovers on Iran-rejection headline

topNews.actionable: The deadline is not confirmed lapsed, but the tone from both sides points toward a binary, volatile resolution early this week rather than a quiet rollover.
